review_log: P3 b-autobot A3 3 -> 2: anchor 3 requires executable contracts AND measured budgets asserted against. The 91 BDD scenarios clear the first decisively; the budgets are comments in a reference.conf timeouts block. blive A3 was docked to 2 for the identical deficiency, so consistency requires it — and since this score flatters the talk's own focal-case story (P3 is the local rehearsal of P8), the conservative reading is the correct one. The paper's brownfield example shows what a real 3 looks like: budgets 'queryable in-loop so that a violation surfaced during implementation rather than at review'.

P6 harp A6 3 -> 2: anchor 3 requires inventories AND data dictionaries AND a glossary, each carrying a status lifecycle. The 759-line DATA_MANIFEST.md nails the first two, but harp's notation lives in the paper (no glossary artifact) and its CRITICAL/MODERATE/LOW/INFO tags mark data-quality severity, not artifact freshness. Both other 3s on this axis (blive, smim) carry a real glossary and real status tags.

P1 blive A8 = 3 UPHELD: the planned drift-audit scripts (scripts/audit_context.py, tests/context/) sit BEYOND the anchor, which asks only for agent-runnable checks plus a maintained warm-up/handoff artifact. Both are present and load-bearing.
P5 smim A3 = 2 UPHELD: blocking acceptance-test doc plus standing assumptions is partial executable spec; no NFR envelope, no incumbent parity contract. Correctly placed.
P2 btest A5 note corrected from WS2 measurement (see below) — the score of 1 is unaffected.

headline_observations: Ordering defies the naive expectation (blive high, btest low, research zero): research projects score mid-high via RESEARCH-NATIVE instruments (pre-registration, notation sheets, kill rules, adversarial review) - the boundary claim refines to 'different artifact types and lifecycle', not 'no substrate'. smim at 20 and harp at 16 carry this after review.

btest at 12 is not flat: stable-ID discipline was real during the SMIM era and measurably decayed after extraction. WS2 quantifies the curve - 0% (Dec-Feb) -> 91% (Mar) -> 96% (Apr) -> 50% -> 40% -> 0% (Jul), trailing 13 commits untagged. Within-project temporal evidence, stronger than any cross-project comparison, and it dodges the confound that weakens every other pairing.

datacli (17/24 at 117 files) = a-la-carte adoption keeping cheap high-payoff elements (gates 3, executable contracts 3) and skipping ceremony (protocol 1) - consistent with the complexity-threshold claim. After review it ranks 3rd, above both research projects that carry heavier instruments.

b-autobot and blive have INVERSE profiles (guardrails+validation vs representation+session) - the four practices are separable in practice, not a package. The review sharpened this: b-autobot's A3 drop to 2 shows even its strongest practice is contracts-without-budgets, i.e. half of one practice.
seamQ shows substrate-as-scaffolding: erected during work, deliberately torn down at publication.

REVIEW EFFECT (S2): two of four flagged judgment calls were adjudicated down (b-autobot A3, harp A6), both toward the conservative reading. The corpus ordering is unchanged at the top and bottom; the middle re-sorts to datacli 17 > harp 16 > b-autobot 15. Note that the two downgrades both moved AGAINST the talk's own argument - b-autobot is the local rehearsal of the focal case, and harp is the boundary case whose research-native instruments the paper leans on.
